- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; cap forecast peak and introduce mild downward slope.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model often ignores sentiment and forecasts continuation; align forecast with sentiment direction even if price is falling.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early days of a new trend (e.g., 1-3 days after sentiment shift); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for early trend entries.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., ±0.2–0.4), model tends to over-smooth; allow 1–2% asymmetric adjustment toward sentiment extremes.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates short-term volatility; reduce forecast variance by 10–20% if sentiment is noisy or uncertain.
